findings.finding: THE SHARED UPRIGHT BODY HOLDS — but only once the palette swap is applied. Composited with the body left white against a green head, it is unmistakably a person in a costume, exactly as §4.2 feared. Recolouring the torso to the head's own green (#4E994E) makes it read as ONE creature. The costume effect was a COLOUR DISCONTINUITY, not a body-plan failure. Judging §4.2 without §2.4's own mechanic applied would have answered the wrong question and killed the shared-body model on a false negative.
findings.caveat: It reads as an upright frog-lizard person, not a crocodile. That is the head being wrong, not the body plan. The real §4.2 verdict cannot be final until a head that actually reads as a crocodile is composited.

findings.finding: The body was generated at the wrong scale for its canvas. Its trim is y10..69 in an 80px canvas, leaving 10px above the neck — a 40px head has nowhere to go and runs off the top. The body must occupy roughly the lower two thirds, and the canvas convention (the base pack uses 96x96 with the whole animal in ~68px) has to be decided BEFORE the body is regenerated, because everything attaches to it.

Vindicated before any crocodile part was attached: the shared body's trim is 40px wide against the bunny's 27px calibration. body_w 40 insets the room by (40-27)/2 * 1.45 = 9.4 screen px each side at adult scale. Had the width term not shipped first, the shared body alone would have walked through the furniture.

Open question for the owner, not mine to settle. The bunny's motif is two dot eyes + a black X mouth + white fur, documented as never-varying. An X mouth on a snout reads as an error, so it was not requested here. §1.1 says the crocodile DEFINES the new contract rather than inheriting the bunny's — so whether the X mouth is product identity or bunny identity is a decision that belongs at this checkpoint.

The tail in these composites reads as lying on the floor beside him rather than emerging from the body. That is my placement, not the art — the attach offsets were computed geometrically, never authored. Real offsets come from the reviewer's attach editor once a head is accepted.

checkpoint_A_decision.pipeline_change: The pack itself is generated with the CAPYBARA-PILOT.md template pipeline (v3 create_character, Dick Bruna style clause, purple keying tunic, low top-down, 96px) — NOT by compositing the Stage-0 parts. The Stage-0 head/tail exploration supplies the identity language for the prompt: protruding rounded snout, small eye bumps on top of the head, dot eyes, green skin, thick tapering tail with triangular scutes. This follows the proven capybara worked example whose layout the croc pack must match.
